identity.title: Complete genome sequencing of Bacillus velezensis ML21, an endophytic strain from mango fruit with strong inhibitory against bacterial and fungal diseases.

content.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing of Bacillus velezensis ML21, a strain with demonstrated antagonistic activity against mango and rice diseases, revealed a single circular chromosome of 3,929,792 bp and 46.5% GC content. Genome annotation identified 3,781 protein-coding genes, 27 rRNA, 86 tRNA, and 5 ncRNA genes, along with 4 genomic islands, 4 prophages, and 4 CRISPR sequences. Critically, the genome harbors twelve secondary metabolite gene clusters. Seven clusters show high similarity (100% or 82%) to known clusters responsible for synthesizing antimicrobial nonribosomal lipopeptides (surfactin, fengycin, bacilysin) and polyketides (difficidin, macrolactin H, bacillaene). Siderophore clusters (bacillibactin, butirosin A/B) showed lower similarity (7%). Significantly, four novel clusters were identified, predicted to encode two terpenes, one lanthipeptide, and one polyketide. Furthermore, genes involved in plant growth promotion, including those for indole-3-acetic acid (IAA; trpC) and acetoin (acoA) biosynthesis, were present. These findings provide key genomic insights into the biocontrol and plant growth-promoting potential of B. velezensis ML21.
